name: Oxus civilisation
title: The story of the Oxus civilisation

text: More than 3,700 years ago, people lived in walled towns in Central Asia, in today’s Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Uzbekistan.
Farmers brought water to their fields of wheat and barley through long channels.
src: The Oxus civilisation was a Middle Bronze Age culture of walled towns in present-day Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Uzbekistan / It thrived c. 2500–1700 BCE
settled farmers who irrigated wheat and barley; extensive irrigation systems have been found at the Geoksyur oasis

text: Craftspeople worked bronze, copper, silver and gold with great skill.
They also made pots on a turning wheel and jewellery of colourful stones.
src: Oxus craftspeople worked bronze, copper, silver and gold with great skill
pottery at Altyn Depe was turned on the wheel / jewellery of semiprecious stones

text: Camels were first tamed in these lands, and a little clay model shows a cart pulled by a camel.
Model carts from about 5,000 years ago are the oldest sign of wheels in Central Asia.
src: Camels were domesticated within the BMAC, and a model of a camel-drawn cart of about 2200 BCE was found at Altyn Depe
Models of two-wheeled carts from about 3000 BCE found at Altyn Depe are the earliest evidence of wheeled transport in Central Asia

text: Their towns traded with the Indus Valley, Iran and the lands by the Persian Gulf.
At Gonur Depe, the biggest town, archaeologists found a seal from the Indus Valley with an elephant on it.
src: its towns traded with the Indus Valley, the Iranian Plateau and the Persian Gulf
Gonur Depe, in the Murghab delta of southern Turkmenistan, was the largest settlement / at Gonur Depe an Elamite-type cylinder seal and a Harappan seal stamped with an elephant and Indus script

text: About 3,900 years ago the walled towns shrank, and herders from the grasslands to the north mixed with the people.
The people lived on, and the Tajiks of today are among their descendants.
src: Around 1900 BCE the walled centres shrank sharply / After about 1900 BCE its centres shrank and its people mixed with incoming steppe herders
The people did not vanish / modern Tajiks and Yaghnobis are found to be direct descendants of these Bronze and Iron Age Central Asians
